Subject: MAP kickoff + cost gating questions before commercial review

Hi Kimberly (and Neha),

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked me to lock down the mutual action plan (MAP) around economics so they can sign off at Commercial Review next week. Two quick asks before I take the MAP to our CFO:

1) A short, defensible table showing expected unit cost across realistic operating modes (burst vs steady QPS) — units = dollars per 1M tokens and example per-request costs for our 3 sample flows.
2) Clarify assumptions on cache hit rate (KV/prefix caching) and batching window you used; procurement is worried batching will break latency targets.

We don't need a full audit, just a stress-tested set of scenarios we can include in the MAP appendix. Ideally something concise we can hand to Finance.

Attaching our baseline traffic profile (small sample). Happy to jump on a 30m to walk through.

Thanks,
Maya

Maya — thanks, great questions. Short answer: we can provide a small set of stress scenarios and a one-page appendix for the MAP that procurement/finance can review. I've sketched a draft and attached two files (MAP draft + short eval plan).

Key highlights (TL;DR):
- Baseline unit cost (our hosted model mix): $12.5 per 1M tokens (seq len distribution from your profile).
- Burst vs steady: at steady 2k QPS with batching window 10ms, estimated $9.8 per 1M tokens due to higher batch occupancy; at burst (spiky) with 0ms batching, ~ $15.6 per 1M tokens.
- Caching: we assume prefix/KV cache hit 45% for the patient summary flow; raising cache hit to 70% reduces cost by ~22% in that flow.
- Latency SLO: for 95th p90 target of 350ms we recommend conservative batching (max 5ms window for interactive flows), plus model variant fallback to a smaller quantized model for non-critical paths.

What I'm sending in the attachments:
- ELR_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx: MAP milestones + acceptance criteria for cost gate (includes pass/fail thresholds).
- eval_plan_summary.md: quick plan for the evaluation window (2-week run) with checkpoints.
- cost-stress-scenarios.csv: scenario snapshots used to generate the numbers in the MAP appendix.

Action items:
1) Maya: confirm which two flows you want in the MAP appendix (we pre-selected: 1) patient-summary generation, 2) clinician triage assist).
2) Elara procurement: confirm target close date window (your Commercial Review date? we'll align the rollout and evaluation so the MAP gate can be met).
3) Kimberly/Karthik/Neha: we'll run a 48h stress sim on your sample profile once flows are confirmed and produce a final table.

If that works, propose a 30m tomorrow 10:00-10:30AM PT — happy to run through the numbers live.

Best,

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + cost gating questions before commercial review (internal notes)

Internal note -> copying Maya so she has visibility into the ops assumptions. I've run quick sanity checks on the draft scenarios. A few clarifying items to lock before the final appendix: 

1) Batching settings we used:
   - Interactive flows (patient-summary): target latency p95 <= 450ms. Batching window: 5ms, max batch size 64, simulated occupancy 0.42 -> effective tokens/$ as Kimberly listed.
   - Async flows (clinician triage): allowed window 50ms, max batch size 256, occupancy 0.78 -> much lower unit cost.

2) Cache model: we modeled a hybrid prefix+KV cache where:
   - prefix cache hit = 35-70% (scenario sweep).
   - KV cache reuse for repeated patient histories yields a secondary 10-20% improvement in token count served.

3) Model variants & quantization:
   - Primary model: 13B FP16 (higher quality)
   - Fallback: 13B int4 quantized (reduced CPU/GPU kernel efficiency offsets some gains; net cost ~12% lower at same throughput).

4) Error margin & safety: we added +/- 18% headroom for I/O and unexpected token inflation (free text inputs). Recommend showing two rows in the MAP appendix: 'Expected' and '95th percentile stress'.

Draft numbers (rounded) for appendix rows — per 1M tokens:
- Patient-summary (interactive): expected $11.9, 95th stress $14.3
- Clinician triage (async): expected $7.6, 95th stress $9.2

I'll run the 48h sim once Kimberly confirms the final two flows. Also added a short note in the eval_plan_summary.md about instrumentation hooks we need (per-request token counters + cache-hit metrics).

-N
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
